text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Two National Bank vice-presidents have offered to resign and may be dismissed for drawing up and signing a 1992 contract on exchange rate guarantees which has cost the central bank HUF 3.2 billion. @

- Tens of thousands of demonstrators held an anti- government rally outside Parliament Sunday afternoon, organised by the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party. Jean-Marie Le Pen, president of France's far-right National Front, a guest of the demo, rejected the idea of European unity.

- Some 5,000-10,000 US troops will be stationed in Hungary and Croatia so as to be in easy range of Bosnia after being withdrawn from that country, according to Washington and Brussels sources who released the information to the New York Times. @

- The Party of European Socialists wound up its meeting in Budapest on Sunday with a declaration that the expansion of the European Union is as political necessity and a historical opportunity for Europe.
- People's Party President Ivan Szabo said that he will reveal a corruption scandal at the start of today's session of Parliament.
- Police on Friday questioned lawyer Marta Tocsik again and froze HUF 130 million her bank account to cover costs of procedures. @
- The presidential board of the Socialist Party parliamentary group decided to accept for debate two proposals for amendment linked to the 1997 personal income tax bill.
- Per capita GDP in 1995 was $4,273, up 1.5 percent from 1994, while domestic consumption of GDP fell by 3.1 per cent compared to a year earlier.
- The State Securities and Stock Exchange Supervision suspended trading of Magyar Hitel Bank shares on the OTC market for five working days.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Parliament will meet for four days this week. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Visiting Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring and his Hungarian counterpart Laszlo Kovacs agreed Sunday to jointly work out an agreement on combating drug trafficking, organised crime and international terrorism.
- The tourism sector recorded a surplus of more than $800 million through August, up from $292 million in the same period of last year. @

- Trade unions and representatives of employers rejected the introduction of the minimum health care contribution and the reform of the social insurance contribution system at Friday's session of the Interest Coordination Council. (Sat.)
- With investment income taken into account, the highest personal income totalled HUF 679 million, the tax authority reports.

- New car dealers belonging to the Association of Hungarian Car Importers sold a total of 38,662 new cars in the first nine months of this year, 2.1 per cent less than in the same period of last year. (Sat.) @
- The Swedish company Telia International has sold its 17 per cent stake in Pannon GSM. (Sat.)
NEPSZABADSAG
- The economic weekly HVG has purchased a majority stake in the CompuServe operator Middle European Networks Kft. (Sat.)
